extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant recipients, institutional grants administrators, fiscal officers, and principal investigators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for determining allowability, allocation, and treatment of costs charged to NIH grants (fringe benefits, pension costs, severance, supplies, publication charges, salaries, leases, etc.). Intended to govern institutional accounting and grant budgeting decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment charging policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment, whether purchased with project funds or furnished as federally owned property, normally should be included in indirect costs but may be allowable as a direct cost if this manner of charging is the normal organizational policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health insurance for trainees
rubrics_metrics.description: Health insurance for trainees and fellows is addressed in the Ruth L. Kirschstein National Research Service Awards chapter in IIB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference only; see NRSA chapter for specific policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefits — leave allowability criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of fringe benefits in the form of regular compensation paid to employees during periods of authorized leave are allowable if all of the following criteria are met:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1. They are provided under established written leave policies; 2. The costs are equitably allocated to all related activities, including Federal awards; and 3. The accounting basis (cash or accrual) selected for costing each type of leave is consistently followed by the recipient or subrecipient or a specified group of employees. See NRSA sections for fellows/trainees leave policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pension plan costs — allowability and funding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Pension plan costs incurred in accordance with the established written policies of the recipient or subrecipient are allowable, provided that such policies meet reasonableness and nondiscrimination tests and other conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points: (1) Policies must meet test of reasonableness; (2) Methods of cost allocation not discriminatory; (3) For accrual accounting, costs assigned per GAAP; (4) Costs for a fiscal year must be funded for all plan participants within six months after year-end (delays beyond 30 days for actuarial liabilities cause some unallowability); (5) Premiums for pension plan termination insurance paid pursuant to ERISA are allowable but late payment charges and certain excise taxes/penalties are unallowable; (6) Pension costs may be computed pay-as-you-go or actuarial per GAAP, with subrules: (a) pay-as-you-go limited to actual payments to retirees; (b) actuarial costs allowable if funded within six months (or allowed extension with equitable adjustment); (c) excess funding may be used in future periods; (d) unfunded liability at conversion to acceptable actuarial method allowable if amortized per GAAP; (e) payments for unfunded pension costs must follow allocation principles of 2 CFR 200.431 and may not be charged to a Federal award if not allocable; (f) recipient must provide equitable share of previously allowed pension costs that revert or inure to recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severance pay — allowability and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Severance pay is allowable only to the extent it is required by law, employer-employee agreement, established policy (implied agreement), or the circumstances of the particular employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details: (1) Allowable only if required by law/agreement/policy/circumstances. (2) Two categories: (a) Actual normal turnover severance must be allocated to all activities or funded via a reasonable reserve; (b) Abnormal or mass severance accruals are not allowable; Federal government may contribute its fair share to a specific payment with prior approval by the Federal agency or cognizant indirect cost agency. (3) Severance pay packages in excess of standard severance contingent on change in management/ownership are unallowable. (4–5) Severance payments to foreign nationals outside U.S. exceeding customary U.S. practices are unallowable unless required by foreign law and approved by NIH awarding IC; similar restriction for terminations due to closing/curtailment unless required by law or approved by NIH awarding IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundraising and investment management costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of organized fundraising and investment counsel/staff are generally unallowable, with limited exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1. Organized fundraising costs (campaigns, endowments, solicitation of gifts) are unallowable; fundraising costs to meet Federal program objectives may be allowable with prior written approval. 2. Investment counsel/staff costs to enhance income from investments are unallowable except when associated with investments covering pension, self-insurance, or other funds with Federal participation (per 2 CFR Part 200). 3. Costs for physical custody/control of monies and securities are allowable. 4. Both allowable and unallowable fundraising/investment activities must be allocated as appropriate indirect costs per 2 CFR Part 200.413.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honoraria treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Honoraria allowable as a direct cost with specialized treatment of indirect cost reimbursement when costs exceed $50,000 in a budget year; unallowable when primary intent is to confer distinction rather than payment for services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment intended to confer distinction (symbolize respect/esteem) is unallowable; payments for services rendered (e.g., speaker fees under a conference grant) are allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentive payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Incentive payments to volunteers or patients participating in grant-supported projects are allowable; incentive payments to motivate individuals to use grant-supported services are allowable if within scope of approved project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Salaries and Wages/Incentive Compensation for incentive payments to employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indemnification costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Indemnification costs are unallowable absent express statutory authority if they would result in indefinite, indeterminate, or potentially unlimited liability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In rare cases where authority allows indemnification cost, it will be reflected in the Notice of Award (NoA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent research and development costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent research and development (IR&D) conducted by an organization not sponsored by Federal or non-Federal awards are unallowable as direct costs; must be allocated its proportionate share of indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cost of IR&D, including proportionate share of indirect costs, are unallowable (i.e., cannot be charged directly to Federal awards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property (invention, copyright, patent, licensing) costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectual property costs are unallowable as a direct cost unless specifically authorized on the grant award; may be allowable as indirect costs pursuant to 2 CFR Part 200.448 and included in indirect cost rate negotiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest — allowability rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest is allowable as an indirect cost for certain assets as specified in 2 CFR Part 200.449 and unallowable for hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Payment—Interest Earned on Advances of Grant Funds for additional details.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRB or IACUC costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs associated with IRB review of human research protocols or IACUC review of animal protocols are not allowable as direct charges to NIH-funded research unless such costs are not covered by the organization’s indirect cost rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory Directed Research & Development (LDRD) for DOE laboratories
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH awards to DOE laboratories will not include the proportionate share of indirect costs for LDRD in accordance with the MOU with DOE dated June 18, 1998.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH will not restrict DOE laboratory contractors from recovering LDRD costs within the total funding included in an award; DOE agreed to waive the Overhead Rate on NIH awards to DOE laboratory contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal services — allowability and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal services are generally allowable (treated as indirect), but subject to limitations; direct charging may be allowable for legal services provided by non-employees where reasonable and in accordance with cost principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal services are generally treated as indirect costs; legal services by non-employees may be treated as direct costs subject to applicable cost principles. Before incurring extraordinary or unusual legal costs, recipient should make an advance agreement with the GMO about appropriateness and reasonableness. Legal costs incurred in defending or prosecuting claims (including administrative grant appeals) are generally unallowable except as expressly permitted in 2 CFR Part 200.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library services
rubrics_metrics.description: General library support is not allowable as a direct cost but may be included in the indirect cost pool; library services are allowable as a direct cost when specifically required for the conduct of the project and identifiable as integral to the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lobbying restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Lobbying costs generally unallowable per 2 CFR Part 200.450, with narrow circumstances where costs directly related to performance of a grant may be allowable with advance understanding; unallowable for State and Local governments and for-profit organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should obtain an advance understanding with the GMO if they intend to engage in activities that might otherwise be considered lobbying but are directly related to grant performance. See Public Policy Requirements—Lobbying Prohibition and reporting/certification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance and repair costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs for utilities, insurance, security, necessary maintenance, janitorial services, repair, or upkeep of buildings and equipment are allowable if they neither add to permanent value nor appreciably prolong useful life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improvements that add to permanent value or appreciably prolong life must be treated as capital expenditures and are subject to 2 CFR Part 200.439 / 45 CFR Part 75.439; allowable only to extent not paid through rental or other agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials and supplies (including computing devices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials, supplies, and fabricated parts necessary to carry out a Federal award are allowable; purchased materials charged at actual prices net of credits; inventory withdrawals charged at actual net cost; incoming transportation is proper part of cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics: (1) Materials/supplies necessary are allowable. (2) Charge at actual prices net of credits; stock withdrawals priced consistently. (3) Materials and supplies may be charged as direct costs. Computing devices may be charged as direct costs when essential and allocable, but not solely dedicated to the award. (4) Federally-donated or -furnished materials used in performing award are used without charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meals — allowability and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Meals are allowable for subjects/patients under study or where specifically approved as part of project activity; working meals for meetings where business is transacted may be charged when consistent with terms of award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recurring business meetings (e.g., staff meetings) should not broadly be considered dissemination meetings to justify charging meals to grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memberships, subscriptions, and professional activity costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of memberships in business, technical, and professional organizations and subscriptions are allowable as indirect costs; some memberships allowable as fringe benefit if per policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules: (1) Recipient/subrecipient membership in business/technical/professional orgs allowable as indirect cost. (2) Subscriptions to business/professional/technical periodicals allowable. (3) Civic/community organization membership allowable if used to support R&D and not advocacy/lobbying. (4) Country club/social/dining club memberships unallowable. (5) Memberships in orgs whose primary purpose is lobbying unallowable. (6) Payment of individual membership dues may be allowable as fringe benefit or employee development cost if paid per established policy consistently applied regardless of funding source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nursery items for research participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowable for the purchase of items such as toys and games to allow patients to participate in research protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant support costs classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Participant support costs are allowable without NIH prior approval if additional cost categories are not requested; classification must be documented in recipient/subrecipient written policies and treated consistently across all Federal awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples excluded as participant support (souvenirs, t-shirts, memorabilia) if additional categories requested. Documentation and consistent treatment required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award (pre-agreement) costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may, at their own risk and without NIH prior approval, incur obligations/expenditures up to 90 days before the beginning date of the initial budget period of a new or renewal award if such costs are necessary to conduct the project and would be allowable if awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If expenditures would require prior approval, NIH approval must be obtained before incurring. NIH prior approval required for costs more than 90 days before start date. Pre-award costs must be charged to the initial budget period unless NIH specifies otherwise. Recipients may incur pre-award costs before non-competing continuation awards without regard to the 90-day rule. Incurrence of pre-award costs imposes no obligation on NIH to make the award or increase the budget; generally not applicable to training grants/fellowships (see NRSA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prizes or challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Prizes or challenge awards are allowable without NIH prior approval if they have a specific and direct programmatic purpose and are included in the Federal award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional and consultant services — allowability factors and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of professional and consultant services by non-employees are allowable when reasonable, not contingent upon recovery from Federal government, and subject to multiple relevant factors and documentation requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowability factors include: (a) nature and scope of service relative to service required; (b) necessity of contracting given recipient capability; (c) past pattern of such costs, particularly pre-Federal awards; (d) impact of Federal awards on recipient business; (e) whether proportion of Federal work influences incurrence; (f) whether service can be more economically performed by direct employment; (g) qualifications of individual/firm and customary fees; (h) adequacy of contract (description, time estimate, compensation, termination). Retainer fees require evidence of bona fide services available or rendered. Recipients are encouraged to obtain written reports from consultants unless infeasible; documentation should include consultant name, nature/relevance of services, service period, basis for fee calculation, and amount paid (may be in invoice or report). See Grants to Federal Institutions chapter for consultant payments to Federal employees and Salaries and Wages/Intra-IHE Consulting for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profit or fee under grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for SBIR/STTR program grants, no profit or fee will be provided to a for-profit organization as a recipient or consortium participant; profit/fee is not a cost under a grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A profit/fee may be paid to a contractor under an NIH grant providing routine goods or services to the recipient in accordance with normal commercial practice; profit/fee is an amount in excess of actual allowable direct and indirect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal costs treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal costs (preparing bids/proposals/applications and developing necessary data) normally should be treated as indirect costs and allocated currently to all activities of the recipient or subrecipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal costs of the current accounting period for both successful and unsuccessful bids are normally indirect; no proposal costs of past accounting periods will be allocable to the current period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and printing costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication costs for electronic and print media, including distribution, promotion, and handling, are allowable and should be allocated as indirect costs if not identifiable to a particular cost objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page charges, APCs, and similar fees are allowable where: (a) publications report work supported by an NIH-funded project; (b) charges are levied impartially on all items published by the journal. Publication costs not incurred during period of performance may be charged as closeout costs unless terms disallow. Publications produced under NIH grant must bear an acknowledgment and disclaimer per Section 8.2 (Availability of Research Results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruiting costs — allowability and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of recruitment advertising, employment office operations, testing programs, travel of employees for recruiting, applicant interview travel, and relocation incident to recruitment are allowable when incurred pursuant to standard recruitment program and staff size is in keeping with workload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where employment agencies used, costs not in excess of standard commercial rates allowable. Special emoluments/fringe/salary allowances to attract personnel that do not meet reasonableness or established practices are unallowable. If relocation costs funded incident to recruitment are charged to a Federal award and the newly hired employee resigns for reasons within their control within 12 months, recipient must refund or credit Federal share of such relocation costs. Short-term travel visa costs generally allowable as direct costs if: (a) critical and necessary to conduct project; (b) allowable under cost principles; (c) consistent with established written policy; (d) meet definition of 'direct cost'. Project funds may not be used for a prospective trainee’s travel to the recipient for recruitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relocation costs of employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Relocation costs are allowable when incidental to a permanent change of duty assignment or when a new employee is recruited for work on the project, provided the move is for the recipient’s benefit and payment follows established organizational policies applied consistently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relocation may include transporting employee, family, dependents, household goods, and certain home sale expenses. If employee resigns within 12 months for reasons within their control, recipient must credit grant account for full cost charged. When there is a change in recipient organization, personal relocation expenses of PD/PI and others moving from original to new recipient are not allowable charges to NIH grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rental or lease of facilities and equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Rental costs for facilities and equipment are allowable to the extent rates are reasonable at time of lease decision considering comparable rental costs, market conditions, type/life/condition/value of property, and available alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General rule: rental costs for each budget period charged to that period. Rental costs under leases that create a material equity are allowable only up to amount that would be allowed had recipient purchased property on lease execution date (includes depreciation/use allowances, maintenance, taxes, insurance; excludes unallowable costs). Lease-back transactions: lease costs generally may not exceed amount that would be allowed if recipient continued to own property. Less-than-arms-length leases allowable only up to amount allowed under 2 CFR Part 200 Subpart E had title vested in recipient; examples include leases between divisions or organizations under common control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research patient care costs — scope and classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Routine and ancillary services provided by hospitals to individuals participating in research programs are allowable; certain otherwise allowable costs are not classified as research patient care costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine services include regular room services, minor medical/surgical supplies, and use of equipment/facilities for which a separate charge is not customarily made. Ancillary services are special services for which charges customarily made in addition to routine services (e.g., x-ray, operating room, laboratory, pharmacy, blood bank, pathology). Incurrence of patient care costs not previously approved and rebudgeting into/out of research patient care category may be considered change in scope and require prior approval by NIH awarding IC. Items not classified as research patient care: patient travel, consulting physician fees, and any other direct payments to individuals (these should be included in 'Other Expenses' in the budget). See Research Patient Care Costs chapter in IIB for reimbursement policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve funds for self-insurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributions to a reserve fund for self-insurance are allowable as specified in governing cost principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also see Fringe Benefits/Insurance and Contingency Provisions in exhibit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salaries and wages — general allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: Compensation for personal services (including fringe benefits) paid or accrued for employee services rendered to the grant are allowable to the extent they are reasonable, conform to established policy consistently applied, and reasonably reflect percentage of time actually devoted to the NIH-funded project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct salary is exclusive of fringe benefits and indirect costs. Guidance does not apply to consultant payments or contracts for routine goods/services but does apply to consortium participants. Salaries of federal employees with permanent appointments are unallowable except in certain circumstances (see Grants to Federal Institutions chapter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Salaries and wages for IHE part-time faculty & outside academic year
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges for work performed on Federal awards by part-time faculty will be determined at a rate not in excess of that regularly paid for part-time assignments; charges for work performed during periods not included in the base salary period will be at a rate not in excess of the IBS except as specified for teaching activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For teaching activities performed during periods not included in IBS, charges based on normal written policy of the IHE governing compensation for such teaching. Sabbatical leave costs may be included in fringe or indirect rate; salary may be charged directly for services rendered while on sabbatical if proportional to service and paid according to established policies applicable regardless of funding source. Sabbatical leave paid by employer combined with other compensation may not exceed 100% of regular salary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for documentation of personnel expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Salary and wage amounts charged to grant-supported projects for personal services must be based on an adequate payroll distribution system that documents such distribution in accordance with Federal Cost Principles and consistently applied institutional policy and practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 2 CFR Part 200.430(i) for documentation standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extra service pay (overtime / overload) — allowability conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Extra service pay (overload compensation) is allowable if institutional policies apply uniformly, defined IBS determines when extra service occurs, supplementation is commensurate with IBS and amount of additional work, salaries remain within established pay structure, and total salaries charged (including extra service pay) are subject to Standards of Documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: (1) IHE must have consistent written policies applying uniformly to all faculty; (2) IHE must have consistent written definition of IBS specific enough to determine when work beyond IBS occurred; (3) supplementation amount commensurate with IBS rate and additional work performed; (4) supplemented salaries fall within salary structure/pay ranges established by IHE; (5) total salaries charged to Federal awards including extra service pay subject to Standards of Documentation (Salaries and Wages/IHEs).
